summary: Electric keys by physical modelling: a hammer strikes a tine, a steel reed or a string, and a pickup reads it. The tine and the reed are decaying beam modes beside a slower tone bar or body; the string is a stiff string with a damper. The pickup is the instrument's voice: a magnetic one turns the displacement into a bark that fades as the note dies, an electrostatic one gives the reed an odd-order buzz, and the string has a neck and a bridge pickup. Hardness, touch and a velocity curve shape the hammer; key noise adds the hammer and damper thumps; a preamp drive, a tone tilt and a tremolo with auto-pan finish it. 16 voices and a sustain pedal. Use it for ballad and soul keys, barking drive keys, reedy buzz, funky plucks and muted staccato.
use_for: Electric keys by physical modelling: a struck tine, reed or string read by a pickup that barks when played hard, for ballad and soul keys, drive and growl, reedy buzz, funky plucks and muted staccato; a playable instrument with no audio input.

parameters.name: Model
parameters.description: The instrument: a struck tine read by a magnetic pickup, a struck reed read by an electrostatic one, or a struck string with a damper read by two magnetic pickups
parameters.how: Chooses what the hammer strikes and how it is read: a tine beside a tone bar, a steel reed, or a string.
parameters.sound: The tine is bell-like and sweet with a bark when played hard, the reed is shorter and buzzier, the string is bright and plucky.

parameters.name: Hardness
parameters.description: The hammer's contact time with the tine, reed or string, 6 ms (soft felt) down to 0.15 ms (hard): a short contact excites the high modes, a long one only the low
parameters.how: Sets how hard the hammer is, from soft felt that touches for 6 ms to a hard hammer that touches for 0.15 ms.
parameters.sound: A soft hammer gives a round, mellow tone; a hard hammer adds a bright, metallic ping above the note.

parameters.name: Touch
parameters.description: How much the velocity of a note also changes the hammer's contact time: at 100 % a hard key press (velocity 127) is about 6 times shorter, and a soft press 6 times longer, than the Hardness setting
parameters.how: Sets how much a harder key press also makes the hammer harder, from 0 % (velocity only changes the level) to 100 %.
parameters.sound: Soft playing is dull and quiet and hard playing is bright and loud, as on a real keyboard.

parameters.name: Velocity curve
parameters.description: The curve from key velocity to hammer speed: speed is velocity to the power two to the setting, so 0 % is linear, +100 % needs a hard press (velocity squared) and -100 % answers to a light touch (square root)
parameters.how: Bends the response of the keys, from -100 % (a light touch plays loud) through 0 % (linear) to +100 % (only a hard press plays loud).
parameters.sound: A soft curve makes the keys easy to play loud, a hard curve gives a wide range from whisper to bark.

parameters.name: Pickup
parameters.description: How close the pickup sits to the vibrating tine, reed or string: at 0 % it is far and reads the motion cleanly, at 100 % it is so close that the response curves and the note barks or growls
parameters.how: Moves the pickup from far away (0 %, clean) to almost touching the tine (100 %, bark and growl).
parameters.sound: Far is a clean, sine-like bell; close adds a bark when you play hard that smooths out as the note dies away.

parameters.name: Bar and body
parameters.description: The level of the slower partial next to the note: the tone bar beside a tine, the reed's body, or the string's second polarisation, ringing about two to three times longer than the main mode
parameters.how: Sets how loud the slow partial is, from 0 % (the tine, reed or string alone) to 100 %.
parameters.sound: More bar gives a long, singing sustain under the quick attack; none gives a dry, short pluck.

parameters.name: Pickup select
parameters.description: String only: which magnetic pickup is read, the neck one (full, round), the bridge one (thin, twangy) or both added
parameters.how: Chooses the neck pickup, the bridge pickup or both for the String model; the other models ignore it.
parameters.sound: The neck pickup is warm and round, the bridge pickup is thin and sharp, both together have notches in between.

parameters.name: Decay
parameters.description: Decay time of the fundamental, the time it takes to fall by 60 dB (T60); the higher modes die sooner
parameters.how: Sets how long the note's fundamental rings, as the time to fall by 60 dB, from 0.1 to 20 s.
parameters.sound: Short times are dry and percussive, long times let the notes sing on.

parameters.name: Release
parameters.description: The damper: how fast a released note is damped, the time for it to fall by 60 dB after the key goes up
parameters.how: Sets how quickly letting go of a key stops the sound, from 8 ms (a hard damper) to 1.5 s.
parameters.sound: A short release is detached and percussive, a long one lets notes ring on after the key goes up.

parameters.name: Mute
parameters.description: String only: a muted string, the decay shortened to about an eighth and the higher partials damped much faster, for staccato
parameters.how: Switches the string's mute on, shortening its decay and damping its high partials.
parameters.sound: Muted notes are short, dry and percussive, like a string stopped with the palm of a hand.

parameters.name: Key noise
parameters.description: The level of the mechanical noise of the keyboard: the thump of the hammer at the start of a note and of the damper when the key goes up
parameters.how: Sets how loud the hammer and damper thumps are, from 0 % (silent) to 100 %.
parameters.sound: A little makes the keys feel real; a lot gives a clunky, woody action.

parameters.name: Drive
parameters.description: The preamp: gain into a soft saturation, 0 dB is clean (the stage is bypassed), up to 30 dB for a compressed, warm overdrive
parameters.how: Sets the gain into the preamp's soft saturation from 0 dB (clean) to 30 dB.
parameters.sound: More drive thickens and warms the sound and adds odd harmonics, then crunches.

parameters.name: Tone
parameters.description: A tilt around 1 kHz: -100 % lowers the highs by 6 dB and raises the lows by 6 dB, +100 % does the opposite
parameters.how: Tilts the balance between low and high, from -100 % (dark) to +100 % (bright).
parameters.sound: Down it is round and woolly, up it is thin and glassy.

parameters.name: Tremolo rate
parameters.description: Rate of the tremolo, the level swing of the instrument's vibrato circuit
parameters.how: Sets the speed of the tremolo from 0.5 to 12 Hz.
parameters.sound: Slow is a gentle swell, fast is a flutter.

parameters.name: Tremolo depth
parameters.description: Depth of the tremolo: at 100 % the level swings between full and silent
parameters.how: Sets how deeply the level swings, from 0 % (off) to 100 %.
parameters.sound: Turn it up for the pulsing of a keyboard with its tremolo on.

parameters.name: Auto-pan
parameters.description: How much of the tremolo is a pan: at 0 % both channels swing together, at 100 % one channel is loud as the other is quiet, so the sound travels left and right
parameters.how: Sets how much the tremolo moves the sound between left and right, from 0 % (level only) to 100 % (a full auto-pan).
parameters.sound: At 100 % the keys sweep across the stereo field in time with the tremolo.

parameters.name: Volume
parameters.how: Sets the final level in dB, from off to +12.
parameters.sound: It makes the instrument louder or quieter without changing its character.
